title: Why queues keep growing
summary: A tiny queue experiment: three requests arrive each second, but only two finish. Matching the arrival rate stops new growth; spare capacity clears the backlog.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare: Capacity
sources.note: Background only. The numbers are an original deterministic example: start empty, add 3 requests and finish up to 2 each tick. No random arrivals or claim about a measured system.

scenes.headline: Why does the queue keep growing?
scenes.caption: The worker is busy. The line still gets longer.
scenes.narration: The worker never stops. So why does the queue keep getting longer?

visual.note: A simplified model · start with an empty queue

scenes.headline: One request stays behind.
scenes.caption: Each second: 3 arrive, 2 finish, 1 waits.
scenes.narration: Three requests arrive each second. Only two finish. Every second leaves one request behind.

visual.note: Add arrivals first, then process requests each tick

scenes.headline: Small gaps become a backlog.
scenes.caption: 30 arrived. 20 finished. 10 are still waiting.
scenes.narration: After ten seconds, thirty arrived and twenty finished. Ten requests are still waiting.

scenes.headline: Give the worker spare capacity.
scenes.caption: Keep arrivals at 3/sec. Raise capacity to 4/sec.
scenes.narration: Keep arrivals at three, but raise capacity to four. Now the backlog shrinks by one each second.

visual.note: The 10-request backlog clears after 10 more ticks

scenes.headline: Match to hold. Exceed to clear.
scenes.caption: Matching arrivals stops growth. Spare capacity clears the line.
scenes.narration: Matching the arrival rate stops new growth. Spare capacity is what clears the existing line.

visual.note: In this fixed-rate model · real arrivals can vary
